item.title: MapQuest was gone for 20 fucking years and came back to fight the surveillance state. What a fucking timeline.
item.description:
Well, holy fucking shit. MapQuest is showing drivers where Flock surveillance cameras are located. The same technology that once helped us find the nearest gas station is now helping us see where Big Brother is watching. Apparently, knowing who's spying on you is fucking radical.
Here's the beautiful hypocrisy: the government and its corporate partners can photograph your license plate, record your movements, and build searchable databases of where you've been. But citizens mapping the cameras? Suddenly, transparency becomes a fucking problem. They'll sell you mass surveillance as "public safety" while quietly normalizing a society where everyone is tracked and nobody in power has to explain a goddamn thing. Funny how privacy becomes suspicious the moment ordinary people demand some for themselves. The people watching us shouldn't be the only ones who know where the cameras are. Surveillance without accountability isn't freedom. It's control with a fucking marketing department. Good on MapQuest. #PrivacyMatters #SurveillanceState #FlockSafety #BigBrother #CivilLiberties #MapQuest https://carbuzz.com/mapquest-showing-flock-camera-locations-october-2026/ https://imgur.com/gallery/8scigm9/comment/2515556119

item.title: Why Texas Voter Lines Are So Long
item.description: 1) Year or so ago Texas got rid of voting machines, went back to paper ballots. Because, you know, "ZOMG! Those darn machines are full of corruption & cheating!" So, now we're handed these long paper ballots, and bubble the stupid thing in with a ball point pen like we're children back in school. This slows the process way down. You hand them your driver's license, they log your name, then they have to print you a ballot. At the place my wife and I voted at, this created a "Haunted House" effect, where you stand in the long line to get in to vote, then you stand in a secondary staging area waiting for your ballot to get printed. The stupid part about that is at the end you feed your paper ballot into a machine that reads it and makes it an electronic record anyways. So, all they did was get rid of the convenient touch-screen machines that sped the process up. 2) They got rid of polling places during an election they KNEW would have larger turn-out. Wife and I waited about an hour to vote. And we beat the rush. The poll workers were having to expand the lines, deal with disgruntled people, etc. 3) They used to have "all democrat" and "all republican" options, that let folks just tick one box and be done. Don't have that anymore. You have to bubble in the whole ballot now. And there's shit-tons of positions to vote on this election. In the past, wife and I would show up to a poll, and it would take maybe 10 minutes to wait and vote. Now it's ridiculous. Every vote counts, so they're doing what they can to make the process as painful and annoying as possible to discourage people from voting. Plus, I'll have to keep checking my ballot to see if it stays. I think they're double-checking signatures or something these days, so if your signature on the dotted line doesn't match your driver's license exactly they might find that as excuse to throw your ballot out. My fellow citizens in line with us were fantastic. Everyone stood patiently. People did not talk politics. They did not yell or shout. There were just casual conversations. The poll workers looked very over-worked and stressed, doing the best they could given the circumstances. They were senior citizens that volunteered, and they deserve some kind of medal of honor.
